sentence: This project provides imaging and chemical analysis tools to study materials used for cancer detection and treatment.
This project studies how the mandible and the cartilage that comes before it develop in normal individuals and in conditions with a small mandible.
This project tests a treatment that uses irreversible electroporation on the whole bladder to treat bladder cancer.
This project studies how cancer progresses and how the immune system recognizes tumors, using mouse models of human cancer.
This project supports and improves a software program that analyzes brain imaging data to pull out biomarkers.
This project studies how an inhibitor combined with an agonist therapy affects immune signaling pathways in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
This project tests whether positive childhood experiences and prenatal resilience predict positive postpartum mental health and well-being in people who have had chronic stress.
This project tests whether estrogenic chemicals cause epigenetic changes in germ cells that pass to later generations, and whether nutritional supplements can correct them.
This project studies how aging and clonal hematopoiesis change the way human hematopoietic stem cells respond to inflammation.
This project develops a way to measure drug levels inside single infected cells using mass spectrometry to understand why treatment fails.
This project studies how Neisseria gonorrhoeae uses metal transporters to take metals from human proteins during infection.
This project tests whether dermal mesenchymal stem cells are needed for skin regeneration and whether their decline with aging impairs wound healing.
This project studies how mutations and outside stressors interact to drive clonal hematopoiesis and its transformation to hematologic malignancy in mouse and human studies.
This project studies how neonatal stress in very preterm infants affects epigenetics and neurodevelopment over time.
This project provides flow cytometry, single cell RNA sequencing and computational analysis to support transplant studies in nonhuman primates.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms behind how neurotransmitter receptors work, and how they support synaptic plasticity, learning and memory in the brain.
This project tests whether cerebellar transcranial direct current stimulation helps language therapy work better for people recovering from aphasia.
This project uses multiscale modeling and simulation to study genome reorganization in cancer and RNA folding in viral mechanisms.
This project focuses on the electrical signals found in all organs, which many therapeutic drugs act on by modulating them.
This project studies protein biomarkers in triple negative breast cancer tumors, and tests targeted therapies in cell culture and xenograft mouse models.
